title: What America’s Adversaries and Allies Hope to Gain at the U.N. General Assembly
gist: Five regional experts preview the 2026 U.N. General Assembly against a backdrop of the Trump administration withdrawing from U.N. bodies, cutting funding, pulling troops and tariffing allies; Iran's Pezeshkian is expected to court the Global South with multipolarity and anti-imperialism messaging while claiming resilience after two wars launched mid-negotiation.

insights.claim: The Trump administration has criticized the United Nations, withdrawn from multiple U.N. organizations and reduced funding, signaling the United States no longer intends to sustain the international political and economic system the U.N. underpins.
insights.so_what: The withdrawal of the system's chief underwriter raises the risk premium on every cross-border arrangement that assumed U.S. backstopping — from trade rules to peacekeeping to sanctions enforcement.
insights.quote: have signaled to the world that the United States no longer intends to play its traditional role in sustaining the United Nations and the international political and economic system it underpins
insights.locator: U.S. President Donald Trump and his senior officials
insights.speaker: Holly Dagres, Raymond Kuo, Nicholas Lokker, Richard Gowan, and Jenny Town

insights.claim: Troop withdrawals, burden-shifting to allies and tariffs on allies and adversaries alike are treated as a single coherent signal rather than separate policies, meaning allies should read U.S. tariff action as part of the same retrenchment as the security drawdown.
insights.so_what: Allies pricing tariff risk in isolation are underestimating it; the security and trade tracks move together, so defense-spending commitments become a trade-negotiation variable.
insights.quote: withdraw some U.S. troops, shift more of the security burden to allies, and impose tariffs on allies and adversaries alike
insights.locator: More broadly, the Trump administration's moves
insights.speaker: Holly Dagres, Raymond Kuo, Nicholas Lokker, Richard Gowan, and Jenny Town

insights.claim: Unlike the Trump administration, Tehran still believes in the utility of multilateral institutions like the United Nations, even though it has been unable to use that venue to end the war — an inversion of the historical positions of the two governments.
insights.so_what: A sanctioned adversary defending multilateralism while Washington exits it changes who writes the rules in U.N. bodies; watch votes on sanctions and technical standards drift.
insights.quote: Unlike the Trump administration, Tehran still believes in the utility of multilateral institutions like the United Nations
insights.speaker: Holly Dagres, Raymond Kuo, Nicholas Lokker, Richard Gowan, and Jenny Town

insights.claim: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian is expected to pitch a multipolar world and the decline of American 'imperialism' specifically to Global South audiences rather than to Western capitals, indicating Tehran has written off Western opinion and is competing for the non-aligned bloc.
insights.so_what: Watch Global South abstentions and alignment shifts at the U.N. as a leading indicator of whether future sanctions coalitions can hold.
insights.quote: will make points that resonate with the Global South about a multipolar world and the decline of what it views as American
insights.locator: Holly Dagres Senior Fellow at the Washington Institute
insights.speaker: Holly Dagres, Raymond Kuo, Nicholas Lokker, Richard Gowan, and Jenny Town

insights.claim: The United States and Israel launched two wars against Iran in the midst of negotiations with Tehran, a sequencing Iran will use to argue that negotiating with Washington offers no protection from attack.
insights.so_what: The precedent poisons future diplomacy-for-de-escalation trades: adversaries will discount talks as a risk-reduction signal, shortening the fuse on escalation.
insights.quote: which launched two wars in the midst of negotiations with Tehran
insights.speaker: Holly Dagres, Raymond Kuo, Nicholas Lokker, Richard Gowan, and Jenny Town

insights.claim: The 2026 U.N. General Assembly opened Sept. 8 with most heads of state arriving for the General Debate beginning Sept. 22 and the session wrapping up Sept. 28, concentrating leader-level diplomacy and headline risk into a one-week window.
insights.so_what: A defined six-day window of leader-level statements is a scheduled volatility event for geopolitical risk assets — position ahead of Sept. 22 rather than reacting to it.
insights.quote: Most heads of state will arrive later this month for the General Debate that begins on Sept. 22. The General Assembly will wrap up on Sept. 28.
insights.locator: This year's U.N. General Assembly officially opened
insights.speaker: Holly Dagres, Raymond Kuo, Nicholas Lokker, Richard Gowan, and Jenny Town
